name: history is the data
headline: History *is* the data structure
visualData: * 0003 | ← the newest marker IS the current state
say: Every change you make becomes a new layer — nothing is ever overwritten. The history of a place is a bag of numbered markers, and the newest marker is the current state. That has a beautiful consequence: undo isn't a trick — it's just reading an older layer. You can rewind any page, restore any moment, name a revision, or snapshot the whole hive before an experiment. Your history is not a log about the data; it is the data. Deploying, backing up, and remembering become the same operation.
